name: Spas and wellness centres

problems.words: Rooms free but therapists booked, or the other way round
quick_ideas: Plan one week matching rooms with therapist shifts, to see where they fall out of step
Note where gaps keep appearing, since those are the hours to fix.

workzap_build.text: a booking grid matching rooms and therapists, with utilisation measured daily.

problems.ask_first: How many treatment rooms and therapists?
problems.free_stops: Grid rules and utilisation reporting are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark each hour this week when a room sits empty or a therapist waits, so the busiest mismatch periods stand out.
Give one staff member the daily room and therapist allocation sheet, so late changes stop creating avoidable idle time.

problems.words: Bookings from hotel desk, website and WhatsApp clash
quick_ideas: Route every booking to one calendar owned by one person, so channels can't double-book
Check that calendar before confirming, so clashes are caught early.

workzap_build.text: all channels feeding one booking grid, with automatic reminders.

problems.free_stops: Channel connections go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every booking clash by source for one week, so you see which channel creates most double bookings.
Make one person record every confirmed booking in one master list, so all channels follow the same availability.

problems.words: Gift vouchers sold with no record of redemptions
quick_ideas: List every voucher sold this season with its number, so you know what's out there
Check the list before redeeming any voucher, so none is used twice.

workzap_build.text: a voucher register with unique codes, sold and redeemed status and expiry.

problems.ask_first: Do vouchers have an expiry now?
problems.free_stops: Code setup and redemption flow stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare vouchers redeemed this week with the sale record you already have, so repeat use and missing entries stand out.
Keep one redemption notebook at the front desk, so every voucher use is marked in the same place.

problems.words: Package sessions tracked on paper cards clients lose
quick_ideas: Copy every active package into one list, so clients' lost cards don't matter
Update it at each session, so the balance is always clear.

workzap_build.text: a package tracker per client ID with sessions used and remaining.

problems.ask_first: How many active packages are there?
problems.free_stops: Tracker setup is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many package balance disputes happen this week, so you see how often lost cards interrupt reception.
Give one staff member the package session list after each treatment block, so balances stay current at the desk.

problems.words: Oils and creams finish faster than they should
quick_ideas: Issue consumables from one person, so usage has an owner
Compare stock used with treatments done, to see how big the gap is.

workzap_build.text: a consumables issue log per treatment compared to bookings.

problems.free_stops: Usage norms go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare treatments completed with bottles opened this week, so you can judge whether product use matches the work done.
Store daily issue notes for oils and creams in one notebook, so unusual product draw becomes easier to trace.

problems.words: Towels and robes go missing and laundry costs grow
quick_ideas: Count linen once this week, so you know what you have
Count laundry out and in on the next run, to see where it disappears.

workzap_build.text: a linen tracker with laundry counts and loss report.

problems.ask_first: Is laundry in-house or a vendor?
problems.free_stops: Count routine stays for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare towels and robes sent to laundry with those returned on each run, so the loss point becomes visible.
Make one person sign linen out to each treatment room each shift, so missing items can be traced quickly.

problems.words: Therapist commission and tips cause complaints
quick_ideas: Write down each therapist's commission and tips rule, so there's one version
Share session tallies before payday, so complaints come up early.

workzap_build.text: a utilisation and commission report per therapist, tips included.

problems.free_stops: Commission logic is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many pay complaints tie to missing session records this pay period, so the main source of arguments is clear.
Keep one commission tally sheet updated by the shift lead daily, so pay discussions rely on the same record.

problems.words: Treatments rung up as cheaper ones
quick_ideas: Spot-check bills against the booking grid, to see whether it's happening
Make discounts need your OK, so cheaper billing stands out.

workzap_build.text: discount and comp approvals with reasons logged.

problems.free_stops: Approval rules stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the treatment booked with the treatment charged on a sample of bills, so undercharging patterns are easier to spot.
Require one supervisor to note every price change in one log, so cheaper billing no longer passes without review.

problems.words: Hotel takes a big share and settles late
quick_ideas: Reconcile last month's hotel bookings with what was settled, to see what's missing
Agree a fixed settlement date with the hotel, so waiting has a limit.

workzap_build.text: a hotel settlement statement and reconciliation each month.

problems.ask_first: How long does settlement usually take?
problems.free_stops: Statement content is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: List hotel bookings beside settlements received for this week, so the unpaid portion is clear before month end.
Keep one notebook for hotel settlement dates and amounts received, so late follow-up stops slipping between shifts.

quick_ideas: Name one person to check each room between treatments, so it isn't left to whoever is free
Spot-check a few rooms yourself, to see the real standard.

workzap_build.text: a turnaround and hygiene checklist with time stamps.

problems.ask_first: How long is turnaround between treatments?
problems.free_stops: Checklist steps stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many room turnarounds miss any checklist item this week, so you see which part is breaking most often.
Keep the turnaround checklist on a clipboard outside each room, so staff finish it before the next treatment starts.

never_say: Anything on hijama or cupping practice or licensing.
Help with illegal services; signs of exploitation go to authorities.
Collecting client health information, names or photos, or therapists' visa details.
Any recording in treatment or changing rooms; medical emergencies mean emergency services first.

sample_reply.person: We sell lots of gift vouchers in December but nobody knows which have been used. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be sorted before the next season. 1) List every voucher sold this season with its number, so you know what's out there. 2) Check that list before redeeming any voucher, so none is used twice. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a voucher register with unique codes that shows sold, redeemed and expired status in real time. Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You can say no.
